items.title: The splitting principle: a projective flat modification making finitely many bundles filtrations by invertible sheaves
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for finitely many finite locally free modules on a locally finite type scheme, a projective flat morphism of some relative dimension along which the pullback is injective on Chow groups after any base change and under which each module acquires a filtration by invertible sheaves, with the corresponding injectivity on the bivariant theory (statement lines 8428-8443, tag 0F5F-adjacent). The proof is an induction on the sum of the ranks minus one: at each step it passes to the projective bundle of a bundle of rank greater than one, where an invertible quotient splits off and pullback is injective, and applies the induction hypothesis to the kernel and the remaining bundles. The induction with its bookkeeping of injectivity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
